# Key Insights (auto-generated from the dataset)

> Dataset: SYNTHETIC call-center data, 59,976 calls, 01 Apr 2026 to 30 Sep 2026.

## Overall KPIs
| KPI | Value |
|---|---|
| Total calls | 59,976 |
| Abandon rate | 5.1% |
| SLA (answered within 20s) | 63.1% |
| Average handle time | 7.5 min |
| Average speed of answer | 39 sec |
| First contact resolution | 75.2% |
| Average CSAT | 3.84 / 5 |
| Repeat calls (within 7 days) | 12.5% |

## Findings
1. **Peak-hour abandonment.** The busiest hours with the worst abandonment are 10:00, 16:00, 17:00, where 7.6% of callers hang up vs 5.1% overall. Bringing those hours down to the overall average would save about **386 calls** over the period.
2. **Night shift is understaffed.** At 22:00-23:59 the abandon rate is 13.7% (2.7x the overall rate) because very few agents are rostered.
3. **Monday is the worst day** (7.9% abandon) and Sunday the best (1.6%).
4. **Retention has the lowest FCR** at 65.1% (best: Sales at 87.0%). Low FCR means repeat calls and more load.
5. **New agents (0-6 months)** take 8.7 min per call vs 6.7 min for 25+ months (29% longer), with FCR 65.5% vs 80.0% and CSAT 3.75 vs 3.89. Better onboarding / call-shadowing would help.
6. **Waiting hurts satisfaction.** Average CSAT is 3.97 when answered within 20s, falling to 2.99 when the wait is over 120s.
7. **Billing spikes in the first week of every month.** Billing gets 124 calls/day on days 1-7 vs 91 calls/day for the rest of the month (36% higher) - staff Billing up around bill-cycle dates.

## Recommendations
- Add agents (or split breaks / shift starts) around 10:00, 16:00, 17:00 and on Mondays.
- Roster more agents for the 22:00-24:00 window.
- Add Billing agents on days 1-7 of each month.
- Fix the root causes of repeat contacts in **Retention** (knowledge base, escalation path).
- Pair new agents with a mentor for their first 6 months.
